ARABIC — TERMLY EXAM #9
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: ARABIC
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Active Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Active Listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening.

2. When practising Speaking Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Speaking Fluency.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Speaking Fluency.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Speaking Fluency.

3. In ARABIC, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day
   B. Avoid speaking to classmates
   C. Only memorise without using the language
   D. Mix random languages with no purpose

4. When practising Reading for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Comprehension.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Comprehension.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Comprehension.

5. When practising Conversational skills, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Conversational skills.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Conversational skills.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Conversational skills.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Conversational skills.

6. When practising Phonological Awareness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological Awareness.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Phonological Awareness.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Phonological Awareness.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness.

7. When practising Intensive Reading: Short Stories, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

8. When practising Imitative speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Imitative speaking.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Imitative speaking.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Imitative speaking.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Imitative speaking.

9. When practising Selective Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Selective Listening.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Selective Listening.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Selective Listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Selective Listening.

10. When practising Reading Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading Fluency.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading Fluency.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading Fluency.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Fluency.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
11. In three clear sentences, explain Numbers and Quantity العَ َدد َوال َمعُدود and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain Active Listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Phonological Awareness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Speaking Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Imitative speaking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Conversational skills and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
